examples.en: There is a lot of wide farmland around here.
They brought river water to irrigate the farmland.

examples.ko: 도시가 커지면서 농지는 점점 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: As the city grows, farmland is shrinking little by little.
My father bought farmland and started growing rice.
A factory was built on land that used to be farmland.
Both the farmland and the houses were flooded.

explain: '밭'과 '논'은 실제 땅 하나하나를 말하고, '농지'는 농사짓는 땅 전체를 뉴스나 법에서 묶어 부를 때 써요. '농지가 줄다', '농지를 사다'처럼 숫자나 제도와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Farmland is shrinking as the city grows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 땅이 줄어드는 문제를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when talking about shrinking land.

phrases.en: My uncle bought farmland in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅을 사고파는 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about buying and selling land.

phrases.example: 우리 마을의 농지 면적은 꽤 넓어요.
phrases.en: The farmland area of our village is quite large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅의 크기를 숫자로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the size of land in numbers.

explain_en: 밭 and 논 name actual fields one by one, while 농지 is the general term for land used for farming, common in news and law. It often appears in phrases like 농지가 줄다 and 농지를 사다.

examples.en: There is a really wide variety of fish species in this river.

examples.ko: 어종마다 잡을 수 있는 시기가 달라요.
examples.en: The season when you can catch them differs for each fish species.

examples.ko: 낚시를 하기 전에 어떤 어종이 많은지 알아봤어요.
examples.en: Before fishing, I checked which fish species are common.
I saw news that a new fish species was discovered.

examples.ko: 외국에서 들어온 어종 때문에 생태계가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The ecosystem changed because of a fish species brought in from abroad.
At the raw fish restaurant, I asked which fish came in today.

explain: '물고기 종류'를 한 단어로 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '물고기 종류'라고 많이 하고, '어종'은 낚시, 횟집, 뉴스, 환경 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 셀 때는 '몇 종'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 시장에서는 다양한 어종을 살 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can buy many kinds of fish at this market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물고기 종류가 많다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing for saying there are many kinds of fish.

phrases.en: The government tries to protect fish species that are disappearing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경이나 뉴스 이야기에서 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This expression often appears in environmental talk and news.

phrases.en: The fishing season differs by fish species.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종류마다 나눠서 말할 때 '-별로'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: -별로 is added when you divide things up by type.

explain_en: It is a single word for 'kinds of fish'. In daily talk people often just say '물고기 종류', while '어종' shows up in fishing, sashimi restaurants, news and environmental topics. To count them, you say '몇 종'.

examples.ko: 올해는 날씨가 좋아서 사과 작황이 좋아요.
examples.en: The weather was good this year, so the apple harvest is good.
They say this year's cabbage harvest is worse than last year's.

examples.ko: 농부들은 작황을 살피러 매일 밭에 나가요.
examples.en: Farmers go out to the fields every day to check on the crops.
If the weather is good, the harvest will also get better.

examples.ko: 이번 태풍은 과일 작황에 큰 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: This typhoon had a big effect on the fruit harvest.

examples.ko: 작황 부진으로 쌀값이 올랐다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that rice prices rose because of a poor harvest.

explain: 농사가 잘됐는지 못됐는지를 말할 때 쓰고, '작황이 좋다/나쁘다/부진하다'처럼 자주 말해요. 뉴스에서 채소나 쌀값 이야기와 함께 많이 나와요. 잘된 해는 '풍작', 못된 해는 '흉작'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Cabbage prices went up because of a poor harvest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 농사가 잘 안 되어 값이 오르는 이유로 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in the news as the reason prices rise when crops do poorly.

phrases.en: This year is a bumper harvest, so there is plenty of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작황이 아주 좋은 해를 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for a year when the harvest is very good.

phrases.en: This year had a bad harvest because of the drought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작황이 아주 나쁜 해를 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for a year when the harvest is very bad.

explain_en: It describes how well crops did, as in '작황이 좋다/나쁘다/부진하다'. It often appears in the news alongside talk of vegetable or rice prices. A good year is '풍작' and a bad year is '흉작'.

examples.en: Today's snowfall in Seoul is 5 centimeters.
The snow depth increased overnight, so I'm worried about the commute.

examples.ko: 산간 지역의 적설량도 꽤 많을 거래요.
examples.en: They say the snowfall in the mountain areas will be quite heavy too.
The news reported the snowfall by region.

examples.ko: 적설량에 따라 제설 작업 계획이 달라져요.
examples.en: The snow-clearing plan changes depending on the snowfall.

examples.ko: 눈이 그쳤는데도 적설량 때문에 길이 아직 위험해요.
examples.en: Even though the snow stopped, the roads are still dangerous because of the accumulated snow.

explain: 일기예보에서 '비가 얼마나 왔는지'는 '강수량', '눈이 얼마나 쌓였는지'는 '적설량'이라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '눈이 10센티 왔어요'처럼 말하고, '적설량'은 뉴스와 예보에서 많이 들려요.

phrases.en: The snow depth increased a lot overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 더 쌓였을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when more snow has piled up.

phrases.en: I checked the snow depth before going to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기예보나 뉴스를 볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when checking forecasts or news.

phrases.en: This region has a high average snowfall depth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역이나 기간의 눈 쌓임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for snow accumulation in a region or period.

explain_en: In weather reports, '강수량' is how much rain fell and '적설량' is how much snow has piled up. In daily talk people say '눈이 10센티 왔어요', and '적설량' is mostly heard in news and forecasts.

examples.ko: 이 파동은 진폭이 클수록 소리가 커요.
examples.en: The larger this wave's amplitude, the louder the sound.
As the exchange rate swings widen, companies are worried.
Read the amplitude on the graph accurately.
I heard the temperature range is larger in deserts.
The market was quiet with hardly any swings.

examples.ko: 진폭만 보고는 파동의 속도를 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't tell the speed of a wave from its amplitude alone.

explain: 물리에서는 파동의 폭을 말하지만, 뉴스에서는 주가, 환율, 기온, 감정이 오르내리는 폭을 말할 때도 써요. '진폭이 크다, 작다, 줄이다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '변동 폭'이라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 기온의 진폭이 커서 옷 입기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: The temperature swing is big today, so dressing is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르내리는 폭이 크다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a big range of ups and downs.

phrases.en: The government tries to reduce exchange rate swings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변동을 작게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to make fluctuations smaller.

phrases.example: 주가의 변동 폭이 점점 커지고 있어요.
phrases.en: The range of stock price changes is growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '진폭' 대신 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday alternative to 진폭.

explain_en: In physics it is the size of a wave, but in the news it also describes how far stock prices, exchange rates, temperatures or emotions swing. It is used as '진폭이 크다, 작다, 줄이다'. In daily speech people often say '변동 폭'.

examples.en: The wave height on the east coast is expected to rise to 3 meters today.

examples.ko: 파고가 너무 높아서 오늘 배가 출발하지 못했어요.
examples.en: The waves were so high that the ship couldn't leave today.

examples.ko: 기상청에서 내일 파고를 다시 알려 준대요.
examples.en: I heard the weather agency will announce the wave height again tomorrow.

examples.ko: 바람이 약해지면서 파고도 점점 낮아지고 있어요.
examples.en: As the wind weakens, the wave height is gradually going down too.

examples.ko: 낚시를 가기 전에 파고부터 확인하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Before you go fishing, it's good to check the wave height first.

examples.ko: 파고가 높은 날에는 바닷가에 가까이 가지 마세요.
examples.en: On days when the waves are high, don't go near the shore.

explain: '파고가 높다/낮다'처럼 파도의 높이를 말할 때 쓰고, 일기예보나 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 그냥 '파도가 세다'라고 하고, 파고는 높이를 숫자로 말할 때 어울려요. 동사 '파고들다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 회사는 힘든 경제 위기의 파고를 넘었어요.
phrases.en: The company got through the waves of a tough economic crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 어려움이나 위기를 이겨 낸다는 비유로 뉴스나 글에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for overcoming a big difficulty or crisis, used in news and writing.

explain_en: You say '파고가 높다/낮다' for how high the waves are, and you often hear it in weather forecasts and the news. In daily talk people just say '파도가 세다', and 파고 fits best when giving the height as a number. It is a completely different word from the verb '파고들다'.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁에서 쌀 한 가마니를 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother in the countryside sent us a whole sack of rice.

examples.ko: 창고에 곡식 가마니가 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Sacks of grain are piled up full in the warehouse.
In the old days people wove straw sacks and used them.

examples.ko: 감자 두 가마니를 사서 이웃과 나눴어요.
examples.en: I bought two sacks of potatoes and shared them with my neighbors.

examples.ko: 가마니 하나가 얼마나 무거운지 혼자 못 들어요.
examples.en: One sack is so heavy that I cannot lift it alone.
The man is walking with a sack on his shoulder.

explain: 짚으로 짠 큰 자루이고, '쌀 한 가마니'처럼 곡식의 양을 세는 단위로도 써요. 요즘은 비닐이나 천으로 된 큰 자루를 '포대'나 '자루'라고도 말해요. 옛날이야기나 시골 장면에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I put the grain in a straw sack.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 담다'로 안에 넣는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '~에 담다' describes putting something inside.

phrases.en: I bought the rice by the whole sack.
phrases.nuance_ko: '째'를 붙이면 통째로, 한꺼번에라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 째 means as a whole, all at once.

phrases.en: I carried the rice sack on my shoulder.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가마니'보다 더 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This word is used more broadly than 가마니.

explain_en: It is a large sack woven from straw, and it is also used as a unit for amounts of grain, as in '쌀 한 가마니'. Today people also say '포대' or '자루' for big bags made of plastic or cloth. It often appears in old stories and countryside scenes.

examples.en: Our house has a building area of thirty pyeong.
Even if the building is big, a small yard feels cramped.

examples.ko: 이 건물의 건평을 정확히 재 봤어요.
examples.en: I measured this building's floor area exactly.
They built a fifty-pyeong detached house.
Building area and land area are different.
The building area was written incorrectly in the registry.

explain: 건물이 차지하는 넓이를 '평'으로 말할 때 써요. 땅의 넓이는 '대지 면적'이라고 따로 말해서 둘을 구분해요. 요즘 서류에는 제곱미터(㎡)를 쓰는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.example: 이 집은 건평이 넓어서 가족이 살기 좋아요.
phrases.en: This house has a large floor area, so it's good for a family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이 차지하는 넓이가 클 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the building's footprint is large.

phrases.en: How many pyeong is the building area of this house?
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 알아볼 때 건물 크기를 물어보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A question for asking the building size when looking at houses.

phrases.en: The lot area and the building area are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅의 넓이와 건물의 넓이를 비교하거나 구분할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to contrast or distinguish land size and building size.

explain_en: It states how large a building is in 'pyeong'. The size of the land is called '대지 면적' separately, so the two are distinguished. Many documents these days also use square meters (㎡).

en: to read a meter; to measure

examples.en: A staff member reads the meter every month.
Someone came by yesterday to read the gas meter.
The apartment management office read the water meter.
They read the numbers on the meter and calculate the charge.

examples.ko: 검침할 때는 번호를 틀리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: When you read a meter, be careful not to get the numbers wrong.
It rained today, so we couldn't do the meter reading.

explain: '가스를 검침하다', '전기를 검침하다'처럼 계량기로 재는 것을 목적어로 써요. 집에서 직접 숫자를 확인하는 것은 보통 '계량기를 확인하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: A staff member reads the electric meter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검침하는 대상을 목적어로 쓴 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most natural pairing, with the thing being read as the object.

phrases.en: Someone is coming to read the water meter tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)러 오다'로 오는 목적을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -(으)러 오다 states the purpose of coming.
phrases.en_equiv: to come to read the meter

phrases.en: I checked the numbers they read on the bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거 활용형으로 이미 읽은 숫자를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form describes numbers that have already been read.
phrases.en_equiv: the numbers read from the meter

explain_en: It takes the thing measured by a meter as its object, as in '가스를 검침하다' or '전기를 검침하다'. When you check the numbers yourself at home, people usually say '계량기를 확인하다'.

examples.en: In winter, the sharp drop in customers makes things hard for the shop.

examples.ko: 출산율 격감이 큰 사회 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: The sharp fall in the birth rate is becoming a big social problem.
I'm very worried because of the sharp drop in sales.

examples.ko: 수출 격감은 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
examples.en: A sharp drop in exports often comes up in economic news.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 인구 격감에 시청이 대책을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The city hall is looking for measures against the sudden sharp fall in population.

examples.ko: 판매량의 격감을 막기 위해 할인 행사를 해요.
examples.en: They are holding a sale to stop sales volume from plunging.

explain: '급감'과 거의 같아요. 숫자나 양이 갑자기 크게 줄 때 쓰고, 매출·인구·수출 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '급증'이에요.

phrases.en: In summer the number of tourists drops sharply, so the shop is quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격감'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 격감; it appears even more often in news.

phrases.en: In the countryside, the sharp drop in population is a big problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인구' 뒤에 붙여 사람 수가 크게 준 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put after '인구' to describe a big fall in the number of people.

phrases.en: The number of customers has dropped a lot this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '격감' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday conversation people say this instead of 격감.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '급감'. It is used when a number or amount suddenly drops a lot, and goes well with words like sales, population and exports. The opposite is '급증'.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 괄목상대할 만큼 실력이 늘었어요.
examples.en: That student's skills have improved so much it's astonishing.

examples.ko: 몇 년 사이 도시가 괄목상대한 발전을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: In just a few years, the city achieved remarkable development.
This growth is a perfect fit for the phrase 'astonishing improvement.'
In just three months, he showed a dramatic change.
Our team's results have improved remarkably.
That player improved so remarkably that everyone was surprised.

explain: 한동안 못 본 사이에 실력이나 상황이 눈이 번쩍 뜨일 만큼 좋아졌을 때 써요. '괄목상대할 만한 성장'처럼 쓰고, 칭찬하는 말이라 나빠지는 변화에는 쓰지 않아요. 주로 글이나 뉴스, 연설에서 보이는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 올해 우리 팀은 괄목상대한 성장을 보였어요.
phrases.en: This year our team showed remarkable growth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관형형으로 써서 놀랄 만한 발전을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: In modifier form, it describes astonishing progress.

phrases.example: 짧은 시간에 한국어 실력이 괄목상대할 만해요.
phrases.en: Your Korean has improved remarkably in a short time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬하는 말로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used often as praise.

phrases.example: 석 달 만에 그의 실력이 괄목상대했어요.
phrases.en: His skills improved astonishingly in three months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 달라진 모습을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the past tense, it confirms a notable change.

explain_en: Use it when someone's skill or situation has improved so much since you last saw it that it makes you take a second look. It appears in patterns like '괄목상대할 만한 성장'. It is praise, so it isn't used for changes for the worse, and it appears mostly in writing, news and speeches.

examples.en: This year's budget hasn't been decided yet.

examples.ko: 금년도 신입 사원 모집이 곧 시작돼요.
examples.en: Recruitment of this year's new employees will start soon.
There are two hundred graduates this year in total.

examples.ko: 이 장학금은 금년도에 입학한 학생에게만 줘요.
examples.en: This scholarship is given only to students who entered this year.

examples.ko: 금년도 목표를 달성하려면 더 노력해야 해요.
examples.en: To reach this year's goal, we have to try harder.

examples.ko: 금년도 세금 신고를 아직 못 했어요.
examples.en: I haven't filed my taxes for this year yet.

explain: '올해'와 같은 뜻이지만 공지, 공문서, 뉴스처럼 딱딱한 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '올해'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: This year, I want to travel a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but the easy word for everyday talk.

phrases.en: The snow came early this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '금년도'보다 짧고 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 금년도 and somewhat formal.

phrases.en: We will announce this year's business plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공지나 보고서에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in notices and reports.

explain_en: It means the same as '올해', but it appears in notices, official documents and news, which sound stiff. In everyday talk, '올해' is more natural.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 노령층도 쓰기 쉽게 만들었어요.
examples.en: This app was made so that even older people can use it easily.
A free course for seniors is being held.

examples.ko: 노령층의 일자리 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The job problems of the elderly often come up in the news.
This area has a high proportion of older residents.
It's a drama that is popular with older viewers.
Among the elderly, health care is especially important.

explain: '노인'은 한 사람도 가리키지만 '노령층'은 나이 많은 사람들의 집단을 가리켜서 통계나 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요. '고령층'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: The elderly population is growing every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통계나 뉴스에서 나이 든 사람들의 수를 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in statistics and news to talk about the number of older people.

phrases.en: It is a shop that many elderly customers visit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노령층'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly interchangeable with 노령층.

phrases.en: This service is popular among the elderly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에게'를 붙여 대상을 나타내는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle 에게 marks the target group.

explain_en: '노인' can point to a single person, but '노령층' refers to older people as a group, so it often appears in statistics and policy talk. '고령층' is used with a similar meaning.

examples.en: The negotiations have been at a standstill for months.
Sales are stagnant, so we need a new strategy.
If the economy stagnates, it's hard for jobs to increase too.

examples.ko: 두 나라 관계가 답보하다가 다시 움직이기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries stalled, then started moving again.
You shouldn't give up just because your grades are stuck.
Because construction stalled, moving in was delayed.

explain: 발전 없이 같은 자리에 머무른다는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서는 '답보 상태에 빠지다'라는 형태로 더 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '제자리걸음이다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The talks are at a standstill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing most often seen in news.

phrases.en: My grades have been stuck for months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발전 없이 계속 머물러 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means staying put with no progress.

phrases.en: My skills are making no progress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 답보하다 대신 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural everyday substitute for 답보하다.

explain_en: It means staying in the same place without progress, and in the news it more often appears in the form '답보 상태에 빠지다'. In daily conversation '제자리걸음이다' sounds more natural.
